subject: Taxes
title: The Free-Rider Problem
description: A quick win: understand The Free-Rider Problem.

hook.text: The Free-Rider Problem: a surprising example shows why better reasoning matters.

buildup.text: The free-rider problem is economics' oldest dilemma: public goods are available to everyone.

discovery.text: Experiments show people start cooperating in tax games but defect once they see others cheating.

twist.text: The solution isn't punishment alone—it's visibility. When people see others paying, they pay too.

climax.text: Tax systems survive because most people are conditional cooperators: they'll pay if they believe others are paying too.

punchline.text: People pay if others pay. One cheater can break the chain.

quiz.question: What makes most people continue paying taxes?
options: Believing that others are also paying their share
